ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left side is a benzene ring, with alternating double bonds drawn inside the ring; the upper-right position of the benzene ring is connected to a carbon bearing an R1 substituent; this carbon is further connected to the imine/iminium carbon on the right side. The right-side carbon also connects R2, and is connected to positively charged NH2. The lower-right position of the benzene ring is also connected to an NH2. There are curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows; hydrogen-related bonds are also not counted. Reasoning count: According to the specified method, divide the structure into the benzene ring and the external transition-state fragment. There are altogether 6 bonds between non-hydrogen atoms around the benzene ring. The non-hydrogen bonds outside the benzene ring are: aryl carbon–C(R1), C(R1)–R1, C(R1)–iminium carbon, iminium carbon–R2, iminium carbon=N(H2)+, lower aryl carbon–NH2, altogether 6. Total = 6 + 6 = 12.

method.method_draft: Visually split the structure into the aromatic ring and the attached transition-state fragment. Count 6 non-hydrogen bonds around the benzene ring. Then count the non-hydrogen bonds outside the benzene ring: aryl carbon–C(R1), C(R1)–R1, C(R1)–iminium carbon, iminium carbon–R2, iminium carbon=N(H2)+, and lower aryl carbon–NH2. Add these 6 external bonds to the 6 benzene-ring bonds to obtain 12.
